why: rules.yaml records precision evidence per estate under `checked:`. This maps every estate name that may appear there to the language it is written in, so a `checked` entry naming an estate in another language is caught mechanically. A search forward from a rule id can land on the next rule's `checked:` block and give it another rule's samples. Real estates are polyglot and the map must say so; narrower entries make the control cry wolf, which is the failure mode that gets a control switched off.
